found_values.value: At most 9 frames in a 400 ms stall and at most 8 in a 3 ms stall. Outside the start-up self-test the panel keeps one request outstanding (start() refuses a request while one is pending) and waits for its answer until that request's own 1000 ms timeout, so a stall under 1000 ms receives one request's frames at most: 8, a 32-register write at 4 registers a frame. During the 1200 ms start-up self-test the panel sends one probe or one status request at a time and sends the next once the last is 50 ms old and unanswered; the IO board's controller still acknowledges in hardware during the stall, so nothing is retransmitted. 400 ms then holds at most 9 frames (50 ms apart, with at most one shorter gap of about 22 ms, the 20 ms receive wait plus the 2 ms delay, between the last probe and the next status request: 10 frames would need 8 x 50 + 22 = 422 ms); 3 ms holds 1 self-test frame, or 8 from one write.

found_values.value: At most 11,495 frames in a 400 ms stall and at most 87 in a 3 ms stall: the bound of a saturated bus at V20's CAN FD with V21's rates. The tree defines no traffic on the port. The shortest frame counted is a CAN FD base-format frame (11-bit identifier; DroneCAN uses 29-bit identifiers only but may share a bus with protocols on 11-bit identifiers) with no data and bit-rate switching: SOF, 11 identifier bits, RRS, IDE, FDF and res are 16 bits at 1000 kbit/s; BRS, ESI, 4 DLC bits, the 4-bit stuff count (3 Gray-coded bits and parity), the 17-bit CRC, 6 fixed stuff bits and the CRC delimiter are 34 bits counted at 5000 kbit/s; ACK slot, ACK delimiter, 7 EOF and 3 intermission bits are 12 bits at 1000 kbit/s. 28 us + 6.8 us = 34.8 us is a lower bound on the frame time: the rate switches at the sample points of BRS and of the CRC delimiter, and dynamic stuff bits are left out, both of which lengthen a real frame. 400,000/34.8 = 11,494.3 and 3,000/34.8 = 86.2, each plus one for a frame that ends inside the window. Derived from the field layout; ISO 11898-1 was not read. A 29-bit FD frame (19 nominal bits more) takes at least 53.8 us: 7,435 and 56; a classic 0-byte base frame 47 us: 8,511 and 64.

With the enable node's 185 ms upper bound and the 10 ms reserve it meets the 200 ms deadline: 185 + 5 + 10 = 200 ms. CAN FD, which also carries classic CAN. The tree names no protocol for the port. The only CAN application protocol it names is DroneCAN (README.md:110, STATUS.md:383), which defines a classic CAN transport (4.1) and a CAN FD transport (4.4: 'DroneCAN operates on CANFD', 'frames can be up to 64 bytes in length'). A CAN FD controller and transceiver run both.

Nominal 1000 kbit/s; CAN FD data phase 5000 kbit/s. DroneCAN's highest recommended bit rate is 1000 kbit/s (section 8 table), and its CAN FD transport uses 'a nominal bit rate of 1MBps, with payload switching to 1, 2, 4, 5 or 8 MBit depending on hardware capabilities' (4.4). 5000 kbit/s is the highest data rate the transceivers read certify for full networks (TCAN3413: 'CAN FD networks up to 5 megabits per second (Mbps). Up to 8 Mbps operation in simpler networks is possible'); 8 Mbit/s is not taken.

found_values.value: 0 V: not isolated. DroneCAN's connectors carry the bus ground: on the D-Sub, CAN Ground (pin 3) 'Must be interconnected with Ground (pin 6) within the device'; the M8 carries Ground on pin 5 and the Micro connector on pin 4. The tree states no isolation for the port.

+30 V DC on CANH and CANL at least, before any round 2 connector protection. DroneCAN's D-Sub and M8 connectors carry bus power beside CAN High and CAN Low: 'Devices that deliver power to the bus are required to provide 23.0-30.0 V on the bus power line, 24 V nominal', so a CAN line shorted to it sees up to 30.0 V. The Micro connector's bus power is 5.0 to 5.5 V. The port's connector is a round 2 choice, so the highest of the three is taken. The bench's 67.2 V pack (F15) is not on the port's connector.

5.5 V DC at least on CANH and CANL. The only other conductor voltage on the link cable is the display's 5 V supply (F6; IOBoard.md:56, :177), taken from the IO board's 5 V rail, whose tolerance is open (V100), and the highest voltage the display takes at no load is open (V81). 5.5 V is the top of the 5.0 to 5.5 V that DroneCAN requires of a 5 V bus-power line carried beside CAN High and CAN Low (Micro connector), the only published figure found for that arrangement; the link is not a DroneCAN bus, so the figure is taken by analogy. found_values.value: Under +/-5,000 ppm (+/-0.5 %), temperature and ageing included, with the display's clock taken at the opposite limit. Two sources bound it and the value is the stricter. (1) The tree's rule: 'two nodes that disagree by 1% agree on short frames and fail on long ones' (can_timing.h:17-20). A disagreement under 1 % with the two clocks at opposite limits leaves each under +/-0.5 %. (2) The ISO 11898-1 oscillator-tolerance conditions for the arbitration phase (Mutter, iCC 2013, conditions 1 and 2, where df is each node's tolerance with the other node at the opposite limit), at the link's fixed 75 % timing (both ends sample at 75 %, docs/Link.md:198-209): condition 2, min(PS1,PS2)/(2 x (13 x NBT - PS2)), gives 5/(2 x (260 - 5)) = 0.980 % at the display's TWAI (20 quanta, tseg2 5, PS1 >= PS2) and 2/(2 x (104 - 2)) = 0.980 % at an 8-quantum receiver (tseg2 2); any 75 % timing gives the same ratio. Condition 1, SJW/(20 x NBT), gives 4/400 = 1.0 % at the TWAI (sjw 4) and 2/160 = 1.25 % at 8 quanta (sjw 2). That bound, +/-9,804 ppm, is looser than (1). The MCP2515 datasheet's 'maximum node-to-node oscillator variation of 1.7%' (section 5.6) is a general statement for that part at its own longest segments, not the link's limit.

found_values.value: +/-3,876 ppm (+/-0.3876 %), temperature and ageing included: the smallest of the five CAN FD oscillator-tolerance conditions over DroneCAN's valid nominal sample points (75 % to 90 %), with the data phase at 5000 kbit/s sampled at 75 % or 87.5 %, a 40 or 20 MHz clock and one prescaler for both phases. Condition 2, min(ps1A,ps2A)/(2 x (13 x btA - ps2A)), sets it at a 90 % nominal sample point: 4/(2 x (520 - 4)) = 0.3876 % at 40 MHz (btA 40, ps2A 4), the same ratio at 20 MHz. At that point with a 75 % data sample point (btD 8, ps2D 2, sjwD 2): condition 1 = 4/800 = 0.50 %, condition 3 = 2/160 = 1.25 %, condition 4 = 4/(2 x (46 + 280)) = 0.61 %, condition 5 = 2/(2 x (76 + 2 + 32)) = 0.91 %; with an 87.5 % data sample point condition 5 is 1/218 = 0.46 %. At the recommended 87.5 % nominal point condition 2 is 5/1,030 = 0.4854 %. Assumption: every node's SJW equals its phase segment 2, the largest the standard allows. With a smaller SJW on another node, conditions 1 and 3 tighten, and the limit for such a node is not known.

report.value: 32 frames in one receive FIFO (FSIZE 1_1111), 31 FIFOs in 2 KB RAM; a receive object is 8 header bytes, 4 optional time-stamp bytes and 8 to 64 payload bytes, so at most 2048/16 = 128 objects of 8-byte payload without time stamp, shared with the TXQ and TEF. Link: holds V16's 9 frames (400 ms stall) and 8 (3 ms) in one FIFO. External port: one FIFO does not hold V17's 87 (3 ms) or 11,495 (400 ms); the RAM holds 87 only if filters spread the frames over at least 3 FIFOs, and never 11,495. V17 is a saturated-bus bound, not traffic the tree defines.

report.value: Fitted: a 120 Ohm terminator on the IO board with no switch. The link has two nodes, the display and the IO board (IOBoard.md:167, :174), so the IO board is always at one end and always needs its terminator (IOBoard.md:176). A switch or an external plug adds a state with one terminator on the bus, 'the commonest way this is built wrong' (testbench/WIRING.md:417-419). None of the ranked transceivers integrates a terminator. Round 2 selects the resistor, and whether it is one 120 Ohm or two 60 Ohm halves with a capacitor to ground (Research.md:28). No page asks for a switch; if the owner wants the IO board placed mid-bus on the bench, that is the owner's call and round 2 adds the switch.
